gates.description: Procedures declared mandatory: scanner-plus-manual (never scanner-only), every finding reproduced or marked theoretical, severity with exploit path, no silent severity-downgrades
gates.command: All four procedure names in session preamble

gates.name: 0.3 RIG coordinate stated before the first scan
gates.description: RIG coordinate stated before the first scan

gates.description: Harness tuple H_secaudit(threat_surface, scanner_evidence, manual_taint, findings_register, improvement) declared
gates.command: Tuple declaration present in session log

gates.name: 1.1 Attack surface enumerated: all entry points listed — HTTP ro
gates.description: Attack surface enumerated: all entry points listed — HTTP routes, CLI args, file parsers, webhook handlers, message consumers, IPC — with auth requirements per entry
gates.command: .rig/security/surface.md with entry-point table (path | handler file:line | auth requirement | input types)

gates.name: 1.2 Trust boundaries drawn: where untrusted data crosses into pr
gates.description: Trust boundaries drawn: where untrusted data crosses into privileged operations (DB, filesystem, shell, template render, deserialization) is mapped as boundary list
gates.command: .rig/security/boundaries.md; each boundary names source-of-untrusted-input and sink

gates.name: 2.1 SAST run: semgrep with the repo-appropriate rulesets (p/owas
gates.description: SAST run: semgrep with the repo-appropriate rulesets (p/owasp-top-ten + language pack) over in-scope paths; raw JSON report saved
gates.command: .rig/security/semgrep.json exists, parses with jq, and its ruleset list is recorded

gates.name: 2.2 Dependency/SCA scan: pip-audit / pnpm audit / govulncheck /
gates.description: Dependency/SCA scan: pip-audit / pnpm audit / govulncheck / cargo audit + container scan (trivy/grype) if a Dockerfile exists; results saved with severity counts
gates.command: .rig/security/sca.txt with counts per severity; Dockerfile scan report if applicable

gates.name: 2.3 Secret sweep: gitleaks detect (git history included for full
gates.description: Secret sweep: gitleaks detect (git history included for full audits) + trufflehog on the working tree; every hit verified live vs revoked vs false-positive
gates.command: .rig/security/secrets.txt with per-hit verdict; a live credential hit triggers stop tier immediately

gates.name: 2.4 IaC & config scan (when present): checkov/trivy config over
gates.description: IaC & config scan (when present): checkov/trivy config over Terraform, k8s manifests, Dockerfiles — privileged containers, 0.0.0.0 bindings, public buckets flagged
gates.command: .rig/security/iac-scan.txt or a 'no IaC in scope' statement backed by file search

gates.name: 3.1 Top-boundary manual taint: for the 5 riskiest boundaries fro
gates.description: Top-boundary manual taint: for the 5 riskiest boundaries from gate 1.2, a human-style source→sink trace performed (read the code, name the sanitization or its absence); scanners don't substitute
gates.command: .rig/security/taint-traces.md with 5 traces: source | path | sanitizers | sink | verdict

gates.name: 3.2 AuthN/AuthZ logic review: session/JWT handling, permission c
gates.description: AuthN/AuthZ logic review: session/JWT handling, permission checks on mutating endpoints, and object-level authorization (IDOR) manually reviewed on the auth path and 3 sampled endpoints
gates.command: .rig/security/authz-review.md with per-endpoint verdicts including one negative test case each

gates.name: 3.3 Injection-class sweep: raw SQL concatenation, shell command
gates.description: Injection-class sweep: raw SQL concatenation, shell command construction, template eval, SSRF-reachable URL fetchers, and unsafe deserialization (pickle, yaml.load, unserialize) grepped and each hit dispositioned

gates.name: 4.1 Findings register complete: every scanner hit and manual fin
gates.description: Findings register complete: every scanner hit and manual finding deduped into a register with severity (CVSS or critical/high/medium/low), exploit path, affected file:line, and reproduction status (reproduced / theoretical)
gates.command: .rig/security/FINDINGS.md where each entry has all six fields; dedup count stated vs raw scanner count

gates.name: 4.2 Severity honesty: no finding downgraded without a written ex
gates.description: Severity honesty: no finding downgraded without a written exploitability argument; reproduced findings cannot be graded below medium without human sign-off
gates.command: FINDINGS.md 'downgrade justifications' section; sign-off names recorded where used

gates.name: 4.3 Fix-or-track disposition: every critical/high has either a l
gates.description: Fix-or-track disposition: every critical/high has either a landed fix (with regression test) or a tracked ticket with owner + due date; nothing critical/high is 'noted' and dropped
gates.command: FINDINGS.md disposition column; fix entries point to commit SHAs, tracked entries point to ticket IDs

gates.name: 4.4 Improvement entry written: one systemic class (missing middl
gates.description: Improvement entry written: one systemic class (missing middleware, absent default, insecure-by-default library pattern) that would prevent future findings

preconditions.startup_phrase: I assume the input is hostile and the dependency is compromised until proven otherwise.
preconditions.bms_bias: A1 for scans and verification; A2 for fix proposals; A3 for report writing; A4 forbidden — findings never leave the session without Gate-D

self_improvement.update_trigger: same vulnerability class recurs 3+ times → custom semgrep rule, middleware default, or dependency policy proposed to kill the class

success_conditions: All gates passed or degraded-with-log; zero unresolved halt gates, zero stop events
FINDINGS.md complete with dedup, severities, repro status, and dispositions
Manual taint traces exist for the 5 riskiest boundaries — scanner output alone never closes the audit
All critical/high findings fixed-with-test or tracked with owner+date
One improvement entry naming a systemic class
Identity closure: coordinate, audit verdict (clean / findings-tracked / blocked), next safe action stated
failure_states: notes: a live (unrevoked) credential or a reproduced critical finding is a stop: escalate to a human before any further action, and findings never leave the session without Gate-D
stop gate(s) 2.3: session halts; human Gate-D approval required before any continuation or outward action
halt gate(s) 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4: no progress without gate evidence
degrade gate(s) 2.4: continue with deficit logged in the Definition of Done waiver
quality_criteria: Startup phrase spoken and the audit scope pinned: repo paths in scope, trust boundaries declared (public endpoints, auth paths, file handling, deserialization), and audit type (full vs diff-scoped)
Procedures declared mandatory: scanner-plus-manual (never scanner-only), every finding reproduced or marked theoretical, severity with exploit path, no silent severity-downgrades
RIG coordinate stated before the first scan
Harness tuple H_secaudit(threat_surface, scanner_evidence, manual_taint, findings_register, improvement) declared
Attack surface enumerated: all entry points listed — HTTP routes, CLI args, file parsers, webhook handlers, message consumers, IPC — with auth requirements per entry
Trust boundaries drawn: where untrusted data crosses into privileged operations (DB, filesystem, shell, template render, deserialization) is mapped as boundary list
SAST run: semgrep with the repo-appropriate rulesets (p/owasp-top-ten + language pack) over in-scope paths; raw JSON report saved
Dependency/SCA scan: pip-audit / pnpm audit / govulncheck / cargo audit + container scan (trivy/grype) if a Dockerfile exists; results saved with severity counts
Secret sweep: gitleaks detect (git history included for full audits) + trufflehog on the working tree; every hit verified live vs revoked vs false-positive
IaC & config scan (when present): checkov/trivy config over Terraform, k8s manifests, Dockerfiles — privileged containers, 0.0.0.0 bindings, public buckets flagged
Top-boundary manual taint: for the 5 riskiest boundaries from gate 1.2, a human-style source→sink trace performed (read the code, name the sanitization or its absence); scanners don't substitute
AuthN/AuthZ logic review: session/JWT handling, permission checks on mutating endpoints, and object-level authorization (IDOR) manually reviewed on the auth path and 3 sampled endpoints

Injection-class sweep: raw SQL concatenation, shell command construction, template eval, SSRF-reachable URL fetchers, and unsafe deserialization (pickle, yaml.load, unserialize) grepped and each hit dispositioned

Findings register complete: every scanner hit and manual finding deduped into a register with severity (CVSS or critical/high/medium/low), exploit path, affected file:line, and reproduction status (reproduced / theoretical)
Severity honesty: no finding downgraded without a written exploitability argument; reproduced findings cannot be graded below medium without human sign-off
Fix-or-track disposition: every critical/high has either a landed fix (with regression test) or a tracked ticket with owner + due date; nothing critical/high is 'noted' and dropped
Improvement entry written: one systemic class (missing middleware, absent default, insecure-by-default library pattern) that would prevent future findings

final_rule: Scanners find candidates; only traces prove vulnerabilities.
No severity downgrade without an exploitability argument.
Critical and high never close as 'noted'.
No improvement entry, no session complete.
Every code-security-audit session leaves the system stronger than it found it.
